govdocs-archive_org-TheHynekUFOReport_Th: Dr. J. Allen Hynek’s Hynek UFO Report gathers the astronomer’s UFO investigations. The Project Blue Book scientific consultant became a believer in the phenomenon. His close-encounter scale is famous. Spielberg consulted him for the film. The book is the classic scientific UFO study.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-BaileyRobert_Ba: This letter to Robert Bailey — June 21, 1977, creator unknown — is an archive item. The file’s full context is unclear. Letters capture voices the record misses. Its subject seems to be the JFK case. Archivists value such fragments. The item is a fragment of correspondence.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-CIALippertRonal: This statement on the killing of Oswald — November 24, 1963, creator unknown — is a file on Ruby’s shooting. Ruby shot Oswald on live television. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of the record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-GaitherReport_G: This Washington Post coverage of the Gaither Report — December 2, 1957 — is a press file on the Cold War study. The report warned of a missile gap. The file belongs to the political archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-GiesePatorCurt_: These handwritten notes on the Pat Wiese debrief — 1971, creator unknown — are a file. Handwritten notes capture the moment. The notes may hold a clue. The file belongs to the assassination archive. The item is a fragment of the record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-LynchReport_Lyn: Thomas C. Lynch’s Para-Military Organizations in California is a law-enforcement report. The AG tracked extremist militias. The report mapped the threat. The report endures. California led the nation. The file belongs to the political archive. The item is a fragment of the record.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-MacNeilRobert_M: Jerry Organ’s MacNeil’s Newshour is a broadcast file. The Newshour was public TV’s flagship. Organ’s segment aired the debate. The broadcast endures. The show was measured. The file belongs to the press archive. The item is a fragment of broadcast history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-MitgangHerbert_: Herbert Mitgang’s Policing America’s Writers covers FBI surveillance of authors. The Bureau kept files on the literati. Mitgang exposed the watch lists. The book was brave. The file belongs to the literary archive. The item is a fragment of press history.
govdocs-archive_org-nsia-PhilbrickHerber: This item — Philbrick, Herbert A. — is a National Security Internet Archive file. The file’s full context is unclear. Its subject seems to be the JFK case. Archivists value such fragments. The item is a fragment of the archive.
petty-troubles-of-married-life-second-pa: Honoré de Balzac turns his unsparing eye on marriage in these satirical sketches — the second half of his comic anatomy of wedded life. Husbands and wives maneuver, misunderstand, and exasperate each other in scenes any married reader will recognize. Balzac's wit is sharp but affectionate: he laughs at marriage because he finds it endlessly, fascinatingly human.
the-clicking-of-cuthbert: Wodehouse turns to golf in this collection of linked comic tales from the clubhouse. The Oldest Member spins yarns of duffers in love, matches won and lost, and the strange power of the game. Even non-golfers will laugh — the master is at his most infectious.
at-agincourt: Henty's boy hero fights at Agincourt beside Henry V — the longbowmen, the mud of the field, the glorious victory against fearful odds. Young readers march through one of England's proudest days, learning history with every charge. Thrilling, instructive, and pure Henty.
the-rising-of-the-court: Henry Lawson's Rising of the Court — bush ballads and stories of shearing sheds, selections, and outback justice — gave Australia its own voice. His verses of swagmen and battlers made him the people's poet. The essential Lawson for all lovers of the bush.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adalbert: This 1913 reference piece on St. Adalbert — the apostle of Prussia, martyred in 997. F.M. Rudge tells his missionary tale. Prague's bishop died for the northern pagans. Poland's patron wears his crown of thorns. Gniezno guards his relics with pride. His martyrdom crowned the Polish Church.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adrian-willae: A 1913 entry on Adrian Willaert — the Fleming who made Venice sing. Joseph Otten honors the master of St. Mark's. His double choirs filled the basilica. Music's Venetian school starts with him. The father of the cori spezzati. His Musica nova amazed the sixteenth century.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-ambrose-autpe: This 1913 reference piece on Ambrose Autpert — the Frankish abbot and theologian. Francis Havey notes his works. His pen served the Carolingian reform. The entry preserves his modest fame. A monk among the scholars. His commentary on Revelation was famed. His works fill the patristic volumes.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-animals-in-ch: A 1913 entry on animals in Christian art — the lamb, the fish, the dove. Paul Cret deciphers their symbols. The catacombs teem with their forms. Each beast preached a sermon. The menagerie's sacred meaning. Their forms fill the bestiaries' pages. Their study delights the antiquarian.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-anselm-eckart: This 1913 reference article on Anselm Eckart — the Jesuit missionary of Brazil. Edward Spillane honors his labors. He served the Indian villages for decades. The Amazon knew his zeal. A German priest of the tropics. His letters describe the mission life.
